definitions.explanation: Publishing a book or other work independently, without going through a traditional publishing house. The author handles or arranges editing, design, printing, and distribution.

examples.japanese: {自己出版|じこしゅっぱん}で{本|ほん}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I published a book through self-publishing.

examples.japanese: {電子書籍|でんししょせき}なら{自己出版|じこしゅっぱん}のハードルが{低|ひく}い。
examples.english: The barrier to self-publishing is low with e-books.

examples.japanese: SNSで{人気|にんき}を{集|あつ}めてから{自己出版|じこしゅっぱん}で{写真集|しゃしんしゅう}を{出|だ}す{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More and more people are building a following on social media and then self-publishing photo books.

notes:
Composed of {自己|じこ} (self) and {出版|しゅっぱん} (publishing). In Japan, self-publishing has traditionally been done through {自費出版|じひしゅっぱん} (paying out of pocket for a publisher's services), but {自己出版|じこしゅっぱん} has come to refer more specifically to the modern model where the author handles everything independently, especially through digital platforms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自己出版|じこしゅっぱん}する: to self-publish
- {自己出版|じこしゅっぱん}の{本|ほん}: self-published book
- {電子書籍|でんししょせき}の{自己出版|じこしゅっぱん}: e-book self-publishing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自費出版|じひしゅっぱん}: vanity publishing — paying a publisher to produce your book; the traditional Japanese model
- {商業出版|しょうぎょうしゅっぱん}: commercial publishing — the publisher bears costs and selects manuscripts
- {同人誌|どうじんし}: doujinshi — self-published fan works or indie magazines, a major Japanese subculture
